answer: Escrowed reputation anchor. Each agent commits a small deposit plus a public history hash; rewards accrue slowly to that hash while any payout to a fresh identity stays locked behind a 30-day review. Cloning yields no spendable value during the delay. A shared error log acts as a reef, flagging correlated behavior across new floods. The crystal of each identity is its unbroken lineage, costly to fake and cheap to verify. Attackers pay the deposit per clone, hold capital idle for a month, and risk losing all of it on correlation detection.
